Description: Tamsapor served in 374 AD as a decorated frontier margrave (Marzban) and equestrian commander of the Sassanid Persian Empire, hailing from the prestigious Ispahbudhan Command House. Serving the majestic autocracy of Shahanshah Shapur II the Great, he commanded formidable squadrons of Asbaran heavy cataphracts around Sassanid Empire. Mastering the martial arts of Iranian chivalry from youth, he was lethal with both the two-handed contus lance and composite recurve bow, armored from head to heel in articulated mail and scale. Steeped in Zoroastrian faith, he guarded sacred fire altars while fortifying Euphrates river bastions and war elephant corps against Roman legionary incursions. This resolute Persian lord held martial honor above mortal life, dedicated to sweeping Western armies from the Mesopotamian plains to seal Sassanian supremacy. Throughout his distinguished career in the Sassanian military elite, he consecrated his life to the supreme chivalric honor of the Asbaran heavy cavalry. An absolute master of equine barding, armor metallurgy, and two-handed contus lance thrusts, he preceded every campaign with sacred Zoroastrian purification rites at the fire altar. On the field of battle, he directed devastating cataphract shock charges that shattered enemy phalanxes beneath unstoppable iron mass. This fierce Iranian margrave stood ready to shed his blood for the Shahanshah, determined that the victorious standard of Eranshahr should wave unchallenged across the Near East.
